properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js is the SHA-2 backend of ethers.js 5.5.x (ethereum address checksums, message hashing) — it ships with both the wave-app client and the smart_contract hardhat toolchain. No direct call site in the application source; presence is what this inventory records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the secp256k1 ECDSA library ships in the Hardhat dev toolchain (ethereumjs-util/ganache lineage), not in the client bundle. It is also the curve this app's transactions actually sign with — see the live chains at client/src/context/TransactionContext.jsx (ethers/MetaMask) and smart_contract/scripts/deploy.js (hardhat-ethers) plus the committed deployment key in smart_contract/hardhat.config.js:8. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped in the Hardhat toolchain's browserify/crypto-compat stack (dep of the ethers/hardhat chain); no direct call site in application code — presence is the inventory question here. Weak by modern standards (single-iteration MD5, retroactive risk class), so its rating is deserved.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Corrected identity: the matched entries are the bcrypt-pbkdf package (v1.0.2), which implements bcrypt_pbkdf — the OpenBSD-style blowfish-based KDF used in SSH key derivation — pulled in as a dev-only dependency of the ganache-core local-chain toolchain (its sshpk/ssh2 stack, alongside tweetnacl). It ships with the installed dev toolchain though no application code calls it; the password-KDF it implements is quantum-relevant only in the Grover sense.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: create-ecdh supplies ECDH key agreement (secp256k1, curve25519, etc.) as part of the ganache-core local-chain simulator and the browser crypto polyfills pulled in by the Ethereum toolchain. No application call site in this repo's source; the code path ships regardless.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped dev-toolchain library tree via tweetnacl; no direct call site in the application code, which is a limitation to record, not a reason to erase a shipped algorithm. Changeable here by swapping the toolchain dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic is the elliptic-curve engine behind ethers.js in the browser (secp256k1 key handling, address derivation, signature recovery). The application's live signing is delegated to the MetaMask wallet, which signs with ECDSA over secp256k1 fixed by the Ethereum protocol — observable here, replaceable only by the protocol.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same shipped-library situation as the Ed25519 entry from the same tweetnacl package: X25519/box is available in the toolchain tree; no application call site found. Classically harvestable if ever used for recorded traffic, hence the X25519MLKEM768 migration target noted by the collector.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: keccak256 (SHA-3 family) is Ethereum's core hash — transaction hashes, account addresses and event topics all depend on it; it reaches the app through ethers 5.5.x. Note: client/yarn.lock (e.g. lines 291, 436, 1996) carries the same @ethersproject/keccak256 and js-sha3 entries — extra sightings of this same asset not in the site list.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 reaches the client through ethers' wallet code path (Ethereum JSON v3 keystores derive their AES key with PBKDF2 or scrypt) and smart_contract through the hardhat/ganache dev toolchain. No direct application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt is the memory-hard KDF used to encrypt Ethereum JSON keystores (v3) — ethers ships scrypt-js in the client; ganache-core ships it in the dev toolchain for local-chain account handling. No direct call site in the application's own code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl's secretbox primitive, 256-bit symmetric AE — quantum-resilient class (Grover only halves the ~256-bit margin), which is why the collector rates it A+; it ships in the toolchain tree regardless of direct use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency of the smart_contract dev toolchain (ethereum-waffle/ganache lineage). Ships Ed25519 signing, X25519 key agreement and XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox; no direct import in the application code — no call site is not a reason to reject a shipped library. Changeable here by swapping the toolchain dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js pinned via ethers 5.5.x / eth-revert-reason in the client dependency tree; it is the same shipped scrypt implementation the algorithm object records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pure-JS hash implementation consumed by the Ethereum toolchain (dep of hash.js, used by ethereumjs for address/encoding hashing needs); dependency inventory records it regardless of direct app use. SHA-1 among the family is collision-broken; SHA-256/512 fine classically and quantumly halved at worst.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Executes in the browser at runtime (Vite-built client), so the negotiated key exchange follows the end user's browser defaults; nothing is pinned in code, and no engines field pins the Node build version, so 'version unknown' is accurate — the PQ outcome is runtime-dependent. Note: the Giphy bearer key read from VITE_GIPHY_API is inlined into the shipped bundle at build time (env-injected, not committed), so it is client-exposed by design but not hardcoded in this repo.
